topics.concept: An executive summary compresses a project or analysis into one page: the decision needed, the key facts, and the recommendation. Executives read the first paragraph and skim the rest, so the structure puts the ask up front. The generator drafts this shape from source notes and enforces a strict length budget.
topics.data_idea: Takes seeded project notes with facts and options, drafts a one-page summary with the decision ask first, and checks length and readability targets.
topics.name: Executive Summary Builder
topics.real_world_use: Analysts write executive summaries so leaders can decide without reading the full report.

topics.concept: RAG status marks each workstream red, amber, or green against its plan, with the color earned by data, not optimism. Amber means at risk with a recovery plan; red means off track needing help. The builder computes status from milestone variance and assembles the classic status table.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded workstreams with planned versus actual milestones, derives RAG colors from variance rules, and renders the status table with commentary.

key_params.thresholds: variance bands for amber and red

topics.name: RAG Status Report Builder
topics.real_world_use: PMOs publish RAG reports weekly so sponsors see health at a glance.

topics.concept: A weekly status report answers three questions: what got done, what is next, and what is blocked. Keeping it to one page forces prioritization; a wall of bullets helps nobody. The writer assembles the report from activity logs and highlights blockers that need stakeholder action.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded weekly activity logs with completions and blockers, drafts the three-section report, and flags blockers older than a week.
topics.name: Weekly Status Writer
topics.real_world_use: Teams send weekly status notes to keep distributed stakeholders aligned.

topics.concept: Meeting notes are useless without actions: every decision needs an owner and a date. The tracker extracts action items from seeded notes, assigns owners, and follows up on overdue items. It turns meetings from talk into accountable follow-through.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded meeting notes with decisions and action mentions, extracts action items with owners and dates, and reports overdue actions.
topics.name: Meeting Action Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Teams track meeting actions so decisions do not evaporate after the call.

topics.concept: A milestone tracker lists the project's key dates, marks each as met, at risk, or missed, and shows the trend: are dates slipping or holding? Milestone hit rate is the simplest predictor of delivery confidence. The tracker computes the trend and forecasts the final date.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded project milestones with planned and actual dates, computes hit rates and slip trends, and forecasts completion from the trend.
topics.name: Milestone Trend Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Sponsors watch milestone trends to judge whether a project will land on time.

topics.concept: OKR tracking scores each key result from 0 to 1 against its target and rolls scores up to objectives. The discipline is separating committed goals from stretch ones so a 0.7 on a stretch is success, not failure. The tracker computes scores, shows confidence trends, and flags at-risk objectives early.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded objectives with key results and progress updates, scores each result, rolls up objective scores, and flags at-risk items.
topics.name: OKR Progress Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Companies run quarterly OKR reviews to align teams on outcomes.

topics.concept: A KPI narrative translates numbers into a story: what moved, why it moved, and what happens next. Executives remember the narrative, not the table. The writer drafts the story from metric deltas and annotated events, keeping each insight tied to a number.
topics.data_idea: Takes seeded KPI series with annotated events, computes significant moves, and drafts a narrative linking each move to its likely cause.
topics.name: KPI Narrative Writer
topics.real_world_use: Analysts write KPI narratives for monthly business reviews instead of reading tables aloud.

topics.concept: A steering deck outline structures the executive update: decisions needed, status, risks, and financials, each on its own slide. The outline enforces one message per slide and puts decisions before detail. It keeps steering meetings about steering, not status theater.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded project state with decisions, risks, and financials, generates the slide-by-slide outline, and validates that every decision slide has a clear ask.
topics.name: Steering Deck Outliner
topics.real_world_use: Program managers brief steering committees from structured outlines monthly.

topics.concept: A risk register lists each risk with its probability, impact, owner, and mitigation plan, then ranks by exposure. The reporter refreshes the register each period, tracks which risks materialized, and highlights new entries. A register nobody updates is just decoration.
topics.data_idea: Generates a seeded risk list with probabilities and impacts, computes exposure scores, tracks status changes across periods, and reports the top risks.

key_params.impacts: cost or schedule impact per risk

topics.name: Risk Register Reporter
topics.real_world_use: Project boards review risk registers to ensure mitigations are actually progressing.

topics.concept: A dependency board maps which teams or projects depend on which deliverables, with dates and owners. Broken dependencies are the most common cause of surprise delays. The board tracks each dependency's health and escalates the ones drifting toward their need-by dates.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded cross-team dependencies with need-by dates and provider status, computes health per dependency, and escalates at-risk links.
topics.name: Dependency Status Board
topics.real_world_use: Program managers track dependencies across teams to prevent integration surprises.

topics.concept: Benefits tracking follows each promised benefit from business case to realization: the metric, the target, the owner, and the actuals. Benefits that nobody measures quietly evaporate. The tracker schedules measurement points and reports realized versus promised value.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded benefits register with targets and owners, simulates actuals over time, and reports realization rates with variance explanations.
topics.name: Benefits Realization Tracker
topics.real_world_use: CFOs track benefits realization to confirm investments delivered their business cases.

topics.concept: A portfolio rollup aggregates RAG status, spend, and milestone health across all projects into one executive view. It answers whether the portfolio as a whole is on track and where intervention pays most. Weighting by investment size keeps small troubled projects from hiding behind big healthy ones.
topics.data_idea: Aggregates seeded project data with status, spend, and milestones, computes portfolio health scores, and ranks projects by attention needed.
topics.name: Portfolio Health Rollup
topics.real_world_use: CIOs review portfolio rollups to rebalance funding across initiatives.

topics.concept: A forecast narrator explains why the forecast changed since last period: which drivers moved and by how much. Executives trust forecasts they can explain, not black boxes. The narrator decomposes the forecast delta into driver contributions and writes the plain-language story.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded forecast versions with driver values, decomposes the period-over-period change by driver, and drafts the narrative explanation.
topics.name: Forecast Change Narrator
topics.real_world_use: FP&A teams narrate forecast changes in earnings prep so leaders can speak to the numbers.

topics.concept: An escalation brief gives a decision-maker everything needed in five minutes: the situation, options with trade-offs, the recommendation, and the cost of delay. Writing it forces clarity about what is actually being asked. The builder assembles the brief from issue data and enforces the one-page limit.
topics.data_idea: Takes seeded escalated issues with options and impacts, drafts the structured brief with a recommendation, and checks completeness of each section.
topics.name: Escalation Brief Builder
topics.real_world_use: Managers escalate with structured briefs so executives can decide fast.

topics.concept: A board pack composes the full quarterly narrative: performance summary, financials, risks, strategic initiatives, and decisions needed. Consistency across sections matters more than polish in any one of them. The composer assembles sections from source reports and checks that numbers agree across the pack.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded section inputs from project and financial reports, assembles the ordered pack, and cross-checks figures for consistency.
topics.name: Board Pack Composer
topics.real_world_use: Company secretaries assemble board packs so directors arrive prepared.

topics.concept: A change impact note tells stakeholders what is changing, who is affected, what they must do, and by when. It separates the message by audience so each group gets only what concerns them. The note builder drafts audience-specific versions from one change record.
topics.data_idea: Takes seeded change records with affected groups, drafts tailored impact notes per audience, and validates that each note has actions and dates.
topics.name: Change Impact Communicator
topics.real_world_use: Change managers send impact notes so reorganizations and system changes land smoothly.
